Mark Plays Nuitai

A blind playtest of the pygame demo by Mark, an invented professional playtester, thinking out loud. His notes follow the episode.

Mark Hi everyone, welcome in. This is the first session of Nuitai, a 16-bit style RPG from a small studio, and I'm going in completely blind. All I know is the name and the era it's dressing up as. Over the next hour I want to find out what kind of world this is, what the battle system asks of me, and whether it pulls me in the way the good ones from that era did.

Mark Title screen. A sunset over the ocean, a little island with a palm tree, the logo in this warm-to-cool gradient, orange on top and ocean blue underneath. That's a nice touch, it reads like the sun setting into the water. Little fireflies or sparkles drifting over the waves. New Game, a greyed out Continue, Options. Let's start fresh.

Mark Text on black. "In a world covered by endless water, people live on scattered islands, venturing across the ocean at their own peril." Then "Colossal sea monsters lurk beneath the surface, unpredictable storms swallow ships, and miracles and oddities are daily routine." I like that last bit, miracles as daily routine. That tells me magic here is ordinary, part of the furniture.

Mark "It is a world as beautiful as it is deadly..." and then "Far to the northeast lies a small, verdant island, untouched by the troubles of the wider world. Here live a warmhearted young cook and a headstrong, devout priestess..." So two leads, a cook and a priestess. A cook as the hero is a fun choice. And "untouched by the troubles of the wider world" is the classic opening line that means those troubles are on their way. If I had to guess, the island doesn't stay untouched past the first hour.

Mark "Kulāiwi Village. The last day of Summer." The macron on the a, the hale, all of this is leaning on Hawaiian and broader Polynesian culture. Last day of summer also sounds like a turning point on purpose.

Mark And here's our cook. Kailo, red bandana, big smile on the portrait. He's talking to himself: "Stew for the wake tonight... cakes and breadfruit for the next island. If I leave now I'll be back before Melia's done her chores." A wake tonight. So somebody died. That's a quiet, heavy detail to slip into a cheerful morning. And something popped up along the top, "Lore page added," with a word that starts 'Ulu. Ulu is breadfruit in Hawaiian, if I remember right. So the game keeps a lore book, and it adds pages as words come up. I like that already.

Mark Then someone yelling, "Kailo! KAILO!" That's Melia. Kailo: "I'm right here. What happened?" Melia: "Those naughty boars are back! Three of them, in the taro patch. They're digging up everything!" Kailo: "The taro? That patch feeds three houses!"

Mark And a third person comes out of the hut on the right. Hina, red hibiscus in her hair, very level stare. "Then stop shouting and do something about it." Ha. Then "I was coming over for one of your taro cakes. I'd like there to still be taro tomorrow." She's dry. I like her immediately. If I had to guess, Hina is the headstrong, devout priestess from the intro, which makes Kailo the cook.

Mark Hina tells Melia to stay and "keep the gulls off the stew." Melia: "Why do I always get the gulls? Let me fight with you." Kailo says it's too dangerous. Melia: "Fine, I'll get some practice with my sling." Kailo: "Melia, put that thing away before you break something." "Aww." So Melia is younger, maybe a little sister or a kid from the village who follows Kailo around. I'm writing her down as Kailo's little shadow until the game tells me who she actually is.

Mark Okay, so the cast so far. Kailo, the cook, our lead. Hina, who I think is the priestess, his friend, the one who gets things moving. Melia, the kid with the sling. And somebody died, there's a wake tonight.

Mark The scene cut to the taro patch, and there they are. Boars in the purple taro. There's an elder up by the big two-story hale wearing a lei, and a market stall on the left. Kailo: "Shoo! Shoo!" The boar: "SQUEEEE!"

Mark "Preemptive strike!" along the top, and a spiral wipe into battle. That swirl transition is very Final Fantasy, but the spiral feels like a wave curling, which fits.

Mark Hina asks, "You do remember how to fight, right?" No or Yes, with No on top and highlighted. The cursor is a fishhook, that's charming. Each of them has two little element icons by their name. Kailo has a fire and a water drop, Hina has a pink flower and a yellow star or sun. I don't know what those mean yet. I'm going to say No. Kailo's a cook, not a fighter, and honestly I'm a new player and I want the game to teach me its rules properly.

Mark "...Really? You lunkhead. Fine, I'll remind you." Ha, okay. So picking No doesn't skip anything, it just changes how she frames it. She's a teacher who'd rather be insulting you.

Mark Oh, a turn order bar. "The faces on the right are who goes next. The top one goes now." And "What you pick decides how soon you go again. So think, for once." So it's a timeline system like Final Fantasy X, where your choice of action pushes you back down the queue. That's one of my favorite battle systems, because every choice has a cost you can actually see.

Mark The command menu is Attack, Cook, Element, Item, with little arrows on the sides meaning there are more pages. Cook. Kailo's personal command is Cook. I love that.

Mark Oh, wait, this is Chrono Cross. Pick Attack and you get three buttons, Y for 1, X for 2, A for 3, and a yellow stamina bar of seven. "Those yellow bars are stamina. Every stroke spends some." "Try a Light attack first. That's Y." Okay, I'm into this. Light, medium, strong, each one costs its number in stamina, and you string them together in one turn.

Mark First light hit, six damage, and another "Lore page added," this time "Lelua." Then Hina: "That blue under your HP is mana. Every hit you land builds it." "Moves like your Sauté and my Heal spend it. Don't waste it." So that's what the seven little marks under each HP bar are. Hits charge you up, spells drain you. Again very Chrono Cross, where your physical attacks earn your magic.

Mark "Each hit you land makes the next likelier. Hold Select to see the odds." I'm holding Select. It shows Y as "HIT", X 93 percent, A 78 percent. So the light is a sure thing and it's meant to be your opener. "Every hit tires you, so you wait longer. Strong tires you most." "But land it and it builds more mana. Strong is A. Go on, swing." I swing, and the boar dodges. "Missed. Strong does that. Don't sulk, keep swinging." That's a good scripted miss, honestly. It teaches you the risk right when you're feeling confident.

Mark One thing I'm noticing, she said each hit makes the next likelier, but when I held Select after a light hit, the odds still read 93 and 78. I'll keep an eye on that. Maybe the bonus is small, maybe the display doesn't update.

Mark "That's enough mana. Open Element and show that pig your Sauté!" Under Element there's a heading, "Lelua," with Kailo's fire and water icons beside it, and one move, Sauté, in red. So Lelua is maybe the name of his style or his school of magic, the thing the lore page was about. Sauté for twelve, a little burst of fire on the boar. Cooking as magic. Sure, I'm on board.

Mark Something odd though. The fire burst lands on the front boar, the lower one, but the number "12" pops up next to the boar behind it. Earlier the 6 did the same thing. That's going to confuse people about who they're hitting.

Mark Hina: "Defend is on the left page of your commands. Press left." "Now Defend. Go on, humor me." The left page has Equip, Defend, and a greyed out Escape. Defending gave her one mana. Then her own command page. Hers is Attack, Scold, Element, Item. Scold. Kailo cooks, Hina scolds. I'm laughing.

Mark Of course I had to try it. Scold brings up a mash meter, three seconds, mash A. She scolds the boar and it starts sulking. "Wild Boar A starts sulking." And then, "Hina is out of breath!" and her mana marks turned red. So a Skill can push you into mana debt, and you pay it back by landing hits. Her red marks went from six to five to three to zero as she hit. That's a clever little loop. It means Skills are never locked, they just put you in the hole.

Mark Kailo's Cook page has one dish on it, Poi. The turn order showed it would cost him a big delay, three boar turns, so with full HP I backed out. I'll try it when it's useful.

Mark Then the boars' turn. "Here they come. Each red bar is one of the pig's hits." A parry meter across the bottom, three lanes, Y, X and A, and the boar's blows slide in from the right toward a yellow zone. "Each bar shows its button. Y is a light hit, X a medium, A a strong." "Press it when it's in the yellow. Closer to the middle hurts less." "Dead center and you take nothing. Not that you'll manage." Wow, okay, so defense is active, like a rhythm game, or the Mario RPG timed blocks. You match the button to the kind of blow.

Mark First two blows, two chimes, "Parried!" both times. The third was a strong one and I was late, took 18. And then a second number, 16, landed on him too, and I didn't see a meter for that one. Not sure where that came from.

Mark The boars curl up and go to sleep, which is their move, and they get "out of breath" too, so the same mana debt rule applies to monsters. Hina's Element is under "Māla Hula," pink flower and sun icons, with one spell, Heal. "You're bleeding on the taro. Hold still, I'll Heal you." Eighteen back. Not a lot.

Mark A strong hit for 41 finishes the second boar. "Wild Boar B falls."

Mark Victory screen. No experience points at all, just stats. VIT, STR, INT, END, WIL, AGI, PER, LUK. Kailo has 20 strength, Hina has 20 intelligence, so he's the hitter and she's the caster, which matches what I saw. Two Boar Hides. Two currencies along the bottom with no words, a cowrie shell and a gold coin, both at zero. Cowries as money is a real thing across the Pacific and Indian Ocean, so I'm guessing shells are the everyday money and the coin is something foreign or rarer. And it said three boars, but I only fought two.

Mark "Eat up. Nobody fights on an empty stomach." And the after-fight page reads "Kailo feeds everyone," and you watch the HP tick up. So the cook heals the party after every fight. That's a lovely way to fold the character's job into the game's healing economy. Then "Element slot unlocked," one grey box and one white box. No levels, no experience, just slots opening. If I had to guess, element slots are how this game grows you, like the grid in Chrono Cross.

Mark Back in the field. Kailo: "Look at this. Half of it's dug up. That's a month of poi, just lying in the mud." Lore page, Poi. Hina: "It's not all ruined. Some of those roots are only bruised." Kailo: "...yeah, bruised taro still cooks. I just hate seeing the rest go to waste." I like that he's practical but it still stings him.

Mark Then Melia, and this hurts a little. "Kailo... I'm sorry. The one that ran off. It went right through the stew on its way to the forest. The pot's on its side, and it's all over the sand." So that's the third boar. And Kailo just says "...the wake's tonight." That pause does a lot.

Mark Melia: "They'll be back, you know." "Everybody knows. The Great Boar lives at the top of the woods, and he's the boss of all the boars. He sends the little ones down to steal taro for him, because he's too fat to come get it himself." Hina: "That is not how boars work." Melia: "Then why do they keep coming?" Ha. Melia's kid logic and Hina's flat correction, that's good writing.

Mark Kailo: "...Change of plans. Nobody's going to the next island today. I have a stew to remake, and if there's a boss boar up there, I'm going to go tell him to get his own taro." Hina: "Then I'll take my cake now." Then, "I'll be at home. When you figure out you can't do this alone, you know where I live." "Be back before dark. Old Pono's wake is tonight."

Mark So the person who died is Old Pono. Writing that down. And Hina just left the party on purpose, and told me where she'll be. That's a clean way of saying "go get her when you're ready." I'm predicting the game wants me to try the woods alone first, find out it's too much, and come back for her. Or at least that's the lesson it's setting up.

Mark "I should head home first, maybe Noelani can help." Lore page added, Noelani. New name. I don't know who Noelani is yet, family maybe, since it's "home." And the music shifts to a track called Kulāiwi, which is the village's name. Okay, I'm free to move. Before I go home, I'm going to talk to everyone in this village, because that's what you do.

Mark First villager: "They say the Callers in Makua talk to the dead. Gives me the shivers." Lore page, Callers. So there's another place called Makua, and people there called Callers who speak with the dead. With a wake tonight, that line doesn't feel random. If I had to guess, Old Pono's death and these Callers are going to meet somewhere down the line.

Mark The market stall is the Grocer. Breadfruit, flour, noodles, pia, pineapple, salt, and then seeds, Akai, Taro, 'Uala, Wheat. Seeds in a grocery means farming. A "Word learned: Aloha" popped up when I opened the shop, so there's a glossary that fills in as the game uses Hawaiian words. The money is called pule, and I have zero of it. I can sell my one Taro for 4, but not the Boar Hide or the Fresh Water. I'm keeping everything for now.

Mark That figure with the lei by the big hale is a totem, not a person. Kailo: "Every totem on the island listens. Tell the Akua what happened, and they remember it for you." "And they get anyone who's knocked out back on their feet." So the totems are save points and revival points, and the Akua are the gods or spirits. That's a really nice way to make a save point part of the world, you're literally telling the gods your story so far. "The party kneels at the totem and tells the Akua all that has happened." Yes, I'll save.

Mark And the save file is named "The Pork Strikes Back." Okay, that got a laugh out of me. Chapter titles on saves.

Mark Next villager: "This island takes people too young. Those kids are lucky they have you, Kailo." Those kids. So Kailo is looking after kids, and if I had to guess, Melia is one of them, and maybe Noelani too. And "this island takes people too young" is a second hint that somebody important to Kailo died. Maybe his parents. I'm writing that down as a guess, not a fact.

Mark The big hale is "The Chief's Hut." Five people inside, a chest in the corner, stairs. The first kid I talk to: "Hi, Kailo! I'm Tutori. Ask me anything!" Tutori. Kailo says "Tutori?" and the kid says "Grandpa says it's short for something. He won't say what." Ha, okay. That's a wink at the player. The tutorial kid named Tutori.

Mark He explains the menu, "Press X to open the menu. Items is your bag, Element is where your moves go, Status shows how strong everyone is, and Party is where you choose who fights." "Under Status you can pick which stance you start a fight in. And in a fight, hold Select on anything to see what it does." Then Kailo: "The... menu?" "And the X button." "Button?" "Grandpa doesn't get it either." That's a light fourth-wall joke and it's in the right place, in the mouth of a kid, so it doesn't wreck the tone.

Mark Stance. That's a new word. Kailo's element heading was Lelua and Hina's was Māla Hula, each with two element icons. If I had to guess, those are stances, and each character has two element colors they can switch between. I'll look under Status.

Mark The Info screen has Quests, Bestiary, Glossary, Lore pages, and Records. "Hear about something from the loremaster, or see it, and a page shows up. Read it if you forget who anyone is." Kailo: "I never wrote anything down." "It writes itself. Don't ask me how." And who to ask: the loremaster for the world, "the kids at school know everything. It's on the second floor of the temple, the tall hale in the grass north of the harbor." The grocer for seeds, "The hunting lodge will sell you weapons and elements for battle, and old Ama by the harbor sells fishing supplies." Fishing. Noted. Kailo: "...Who taught you all this?" "I'm just smart, I know things."

Mark I picked "This is boring" at the end just to see, and he says "That's what Grandpa says when I tell him!" Cute. My one note is that his menu loops right back on itself if you press A too eagerly, I heard the Info speech twice before I got out.

Mark Tutori again, he wanders, "Grandpa says I can stay up for the wake tonight! There'll be lanterns!"

Mark The old man at the top is Chief Ulu. "Aloha e Kailo. Bring your stew to Old Pono's wake tonight. He always said it was the best on the island." "And Hina leaves on her pilgrimage soon. Smart girl. She's earned the promotion." Then this one: "Ever since your dad left on his adventure, you've kept that whole house fed. We all noticed."

Mark Okay, so that corrects my guess. Kailo's dad isn't dead, he "left on his adventure." And Kailo stepped up and feeds the household. And Hina is leaving soon on a pilgrimage, for a promotion. So both the people Kailo depends on, his dad and his friend, are leaving or gone. I can feel the shape of this. If I had to guess, the story ends up being Kailo following one or both of them off this island.

Mark The loremaster. Purple headwrap, wild white hair. "The Akua? Here, that means Lanu, first and last. She's in the taro, the rain, the forest, every green thing on this island." "She used to have the sun, too. Then the priests took in the teachings of Haka, the holy man from the west, and gave the sunlight to him. That was a hundred years ago." "Some of them never forgave it. They walked off into the Lost Woods and became the Maki Sages. They still say Lanu was robbed." "Oh, there are others. Mauna in the cook fire, Moanaku out past the reef. But on Māla Iki, it's Lanu."

Mark Whoa, okay, this is a lot of good lore, so let me sort it. The island is Māla Iki. Its god is Lanu, a goddess of green growing things. A hundred years ago the priests adopted a foreign teacher, Haka, and handed him the sun, which used to be hers. A splinter group, the Maki Sages, walked off into the Lost Woods in protest. And there are other gods, Mauna for the cook fire, Moanaku for the sea past the reef.

Mark One thing confused me. He says "Haka," but the lore page that popped up says "Shaka." He says "Mauna" and "Moanaku," but the pages say "Mauga" and "Moanatu." I asked about Shaka, and he explains it: "Haka, we say here. Shaka, if you're from Kota Emas like the young priestess." Oh, that's lovely. It's dialect. The village drops a sound that the outsiders keep. That reads like the real k and t shift between Hawaiian and other Polynesian languages. And "the young priestess" from Kota Emas has to be Hina, so Hina isn't from here. She's an outsider in this village, which explains a lot about her edge.

Mark Then: "A sailor from the far west who put down his sword and found a way out of suffering, so the priests say." "I light a lamp for him, and I pour water for Lanu. Nobody ever told me I had to pick one." So Shaka is basically the Buddha, Shakyamuni, arriving on a Polynesian island, and the old man practicing both at once is exactly how syncretism works in real life. That's a mature bit of worldbuilding for a game about chasing pigs.

Mark And Mana: "Mana. The current under everything. In the sea, the wind, you, me. In a body that sits still it sleeps. Get up and move, and it wakes." "The priests say the Akua are made of it. A god is Mana that has learned to be someone. Which is why nobody prays to Mana itself. Nobody thanks the tide for the fish." "A dancer rides it, the way you time a push on a swing. Move with it and it adds to you. The old masters barely move at all. A breath is enough for them."

Mark There it is, that ties the lore straight to the battle system. Mana wakes when you move, so landing hits builds it. Hina's Element was called Māla Hula, a dance. So magic is motion here. "A god is Mana that has learned to be someone" is a beautiful line. And "In the south they say you can take it from a beaten champion. We don't believe that here, but I wouldn't test it." I'm writing that down. That sounds like a villain's philosophy waiting to happen.

Mark The elder by the chest: "Pono and I fished the reef together for fifty years. Tonight we send him off properly." The chest had a Ti Leaf in it. The loft upstairs is just storage, candles and incense, nothing to pick up.

Mark Kailo's House, with the sign in all caps for his name. And this must be Noelani, red hair like Kailo's. "I heard what happened. The boars, the pot, all of it. I'll help you cook it. Don't make that face." "So what goes in?" Kailo: "We need 4 Fish, 3 Egg, 3 Coconut, 2 Pork, 2 'Uala, 2 Akai Lau, 1 'Awapuhi and 1 Māla Shoyu."

Mark That's a real shopping list. Noelani: "That's a lot. You fetch, I'll clean up this mess and get the fire going. Deal?" Then "Don't track mud in, Kailo. I just swept." Kailo: "'Ae, ma'am. I'll take my sandals off. ...wait we don't wear sandals." Ha. So Noelani is family, same red hair, bossy in a caring way, probably a sister. I'll call her his sister until the game says otherwise.

Mark So now I've got two goals. Remake the stew from scratch, and go up to the woods about this Great Boar. And Hina waiting at home for when I figure out I can't do it alone. I have zero pule, so the shopping isn't happening by buying. I'll have to fish, gather, hunt. Let me look at the menu first, especially that stance setting Tutori mentioned.

Mark Menu check. Kailo's portrait has the two stance icons, a fire and a wave, with the fire boxed in yellow. Under Element, his first row has two slots now, Sauté, "Hits one enemy with fire. 12 physical fire, 20% burn," and a second one I didn't know I had, WaveGrd, "Take 60% damage in place of an ally." That's why only Sauté showed up in the fight, I'm in the fire stance and WaveGrd belongs to the water one. Okay, that clicks. Two stances, two colors, and your element list changes with the stance you're in.

Mark The Quest log says "The Great Boar" and "Stew for the..." There's a calendar, "30th of Kau," a step counter. And the Lore pages split into People, Places, Food, Gods, Faiths, Arts. People says 6 of 13. Noelani's page: "NOELANI is KAILO's cousin, raised in his household on Kulāiwi, where cousins are raised as siblings. She is a little younger than KAILO and the second eldest of the cousins, so she is the responsible one." Melia's: "about eight years old... so KAILO calls her his sister." Good, so my sister guess was half right. They're cousins raised as siblings, which is a real Hawaiian family practice, hānai and the ʻohana being wider than the nuclear family. I like the game being clear about it.

Mark Outside, I tried the hens on a hunch, and "Found an Egg." Two eggs from two hens. The third one is stuck behind the baskets by the house and I can't reach it. A second try on the first hen gives "The hen clucks. No egg yet." So eggs come back over time.

Mark North is Kulāiwi Forest, and the music is called "Potions, Poisons and Forest Mushrooms." A pond, palm groves, two chests I can see, a red mushroom creature, some red and white masked things by the trees, something swimming in the water, and two wild boars just roaming. Visible enemies, no random encounters. Thank you.

Mark A carved post with a cup of water. "A post for Lanu. I'll leave her a cup of water as an offering." Of course Kailo would. Yes. "Kailo poured Lanu a cup of water." And then nothing happened that I could see. No sound, no blessing. I'm curious if that's flavor or if it pays off later.

Mark The boars are pork, and I need two Pork for the stew, so I walked into them. Two boars, Kailo alone. This went badly in an interesting way. A full chain of light, medium, strong, light pushed Kailo all the way to the bottom of the timeline, six boar turns before his next one. So the turn order punishes greed hard when you're solo.

Mark Then the boars got clever. Boar A curled up and slept for plus 25. Boar B "digs up a truffle," and then "throws the truffle at Wild Boar A" for plus 30. Then A slept again for plus 37. These pigs are a team. I did find one nice thing: when you back out of the Attack buttons with B, you're still on your turn, so you can attack and then cast in one go. And after a strong hit, "Kailo's Perception up!" So stats grow by doing, like SaGa, no experience. That's why there were no EXP on the victory screen.

Mark My parries got good. Light, strong, strong, three "Parried!" chimes in a row, and I think a parry earns a counterattack, because a 36 popped on the boar right after. But a couple of the boar hits landed on Kailo with no parry meter at all, 6, 17, 19. I'm not sure what makes some blows parryable and others not.

Mark Kailo was at 62 of 130 and the boars had healed back almost everything I did. Hina told me, "When you figure out you can't do this alone, you know where I live." That's the game hinting, so I'm taking it. Escape is a rhythm check, "Alternate!", L and R, steady beat. "Kailo gets away!" Okay, Hina. You were right. I'll go get her.

Mark Hina's House. She's packing. "You're still here?" Kailo: "I..." "Wait, are you packing?" "For my trip. I leave soon, and it's none of your business." "Did you forget what you were doing? You're hopeless, aren't you? Well, you need a healer anyway, so I'm coming too." I love that she frames it as him being hopeless instead of admitting she wants to come. "Hina joined the party. While she is in your party, the fallen get back up after a win." That's a nice, plain statement of why you want the healer along.

Mark Back in the woods with Hina, one boar this time. Sauté on it, and "Weak!" Earlier the boars "shift to fire stance" and "shift to nature stance" mid-fight. So enemies swap stances too, and their weakness moves with them. Fire beats nature, I'm guessing, since the boar in nature stance took the fire. That's a lot of reading to do in a fight, which I like, but the game only tells you the stance once, in a text line that scrolls by.

Mark Hina said "Fine. That was good. Don't make it weird." after I parried three in a row. Ha. And Kailo's Poi was greyed out after he'd already attacked, so I think Skills can't be used once you've started a chain. The odd part: a Light hit that the Select window calls a sure "HIT" got a "Dodge" from the boar. That's either a bug or the window is wrong.

Mark The boar dropped a Boar Hide again, no pork. So hunting isn't how I get the Pork for the stew, or at least not from these. The grocer doesn't sell pork either. I'll keep my eyes open.

Mark The right-hand chest had a Noni Pulu. Then the red and white birds by the palms, they're called Papanok, kind of a rooster with a big red crest. Hina's in a guarding pose from Defend, and the Papanok throws six blows, five lights and a medium. I parried every one, and a 25 counterattack popped on the bird. When you parry everything you hit back. Oh, that's cool. That turns defense into offense.

Mark Second Papanok. I made a mistake here. Hina's menu remembered the cursor on Item from the earlier battle, and I fed Kailo her Noni Pulu instead of attacking. My fault, but a cursor that remembers across fights is the kind of thing that bites you. And Kailo's attacks on the Papanok all say "Resisted." So his basic hits carry his element. Hina's didn't get resisted. The Papanok dropped... "Sauté." An element drops off a monster. So elements are loot, like in Chrono Cross.

Mark Now I've got a real problem. The north exit of this forest is up past the pond, and I can't find a way to it. The pond runs into the left edge, the palms box in the right side. I walked every edge I could see. Kailo can scoop up "some fresh water" at the shore, so that's how you refill the offering cup. The area map shows this forest as one small square with the village below. I'm going to try the north edge of the other half of the village before I panic.

Mark That was it. The north edge of the chief's side of the village goes up into a second part of Kulāiwi Forest. So the first forest screen with the pond is a side area with its chests, and this is the real path. Fair enough, though nothing pointed me here. I'd have liked a villager saying "the trail up the hill starts behind the market" or something.

Mark Oh, this is nice. A maze of palm hedges in a square spiral, sandy paths, and four boars rooting around inside it. It looks like a planted grove, like the village shaped it.

Mark Two boars. I'm starting to read the boar fights. When they hit me with no parry meter and the word "Resisted" pops up, that's an elemental attack, the fire stance one breathing fire or whatever it does, and those can't be parried. The physical blows come through the meter. That answers my question from earlier. I'd still like the game to say so.

Mark And then Hina: "Wait. We both have full mana, and we're side by side on the bar." "That means a Combo. Press right on your commands." "It takes every drop of mana we have. Don't mess up your half." Combo! Chrono Trigger dual techs. The conditions are both of you at full mana and next to each other on the timeline, which is a lovely way to tie the two systems together, you have to plan your turn order to set one up.

Mark The combo is called Pōhuehue, "A vine grown and whipped at one enemy for heavy physical nature damage." Pōhuehue is the beach morning glory vine, I think. A note bar comes up, "Grow the vine!", notes sliding onto a line on the beat, up, X, up, X, A. Five for five. And then 81 damage in one hit, and the boar falls. Okay, I'm really into this. Every special move is a little minigame. Scold was a mash, Escape was a steady L-R beat, the combo is a rhythm lane. That's very Super Mario RPG and it keeps you leaning in.

Mark The boar dropped another Sauté. And "Kailo's Endurance up!" during the fight. So far: Perception twice, Endurance twice.

Mark Third forest screen. The palms are laid out like a hedge maze again, and there are birds flitting around it, blue ones and a green one. The fights call them Green Aghoy and Blue Aghoy, little winged sprites, almost like fairies with leaf wings. They drop Green Wing and Blue Wing, and the blue one dropped 49 pule. Finally, money.

Mark The Blue Aghoy throws seven light blows in a row, a quick drumroll of Y presses a quarter second apart. I got all seven and it counterattacked for a dodge. That pattern felt good. It's a different rhythm from the boar's slow strong-strong-light, so each monster has its own beat to learn. That's a real strength of the parry system.

Mark Out of the maze, and this is a crossroads. A big hale with a sign, a taro patch, a sandy road both ways, a pool with a little island and a chest on it, a figure in a straw hat by another chest. The sign says "The Crossroads Inn." The innkeeper: "Aloha. You made it out of the woods. Every road on the island runs past my door."

Mark And the inn sells food. Ginger Tea, "Wakes the sleeping in a fight." Grilled Fish, Poi, Saimin, Egg, Pork, Ramen, Roast Pork. Pork at 15. I found out I already had one Pork, the last boar must have dropped it and I missed it on the results page, so I bought one more, and one Egg to make three. Two items off the stew list. Saimin on the menu is a nice touch, that's the Hawaii plantation-era noodle soup.

Mark There's a cook sitting at the inn, and he explains the cooking pot. "The pot looks for a real recipe first. Noodles and broth make ramen, and nothing else will." "No recipe? It looks at what each thing is: meat, fish, vegetable, fruit, water. Meat and a vegetable make a stew, fruit alone makes a bowl." "Last, if it can't make sense of the mix, you get a dish nobody can name." And salt: "Salt keeps food. Put it with one thing and you get the salted version, which lasts at sea." "Salt with two or more things only seasons. If the pot finds no recipe for the mix, it tries again without the salt, so salt never ruins a dish." I love that last rule. It's the designer telling you they thought about how to make experimenting safe. If you ask "What if it makes ???", he says "Then stand back. Something is about to boil over."

Mark So there's a whole cooking system coming, Breath of Fire style, with categories of ingredient and named recipes. I haven't touched a pot yet. I'm guessing the stew for the wake is my first real recipe and Noelani's fire is where I'll cook it.

Mark North of the crossroads, the music changes to something called "Sapphire Rain Drops," and the sign says "Lanu's Grove." Oh, this is beautiful. A square spring ringed with palms, a carved post with a water cup, a totem with a lei at the side, a few villagers praying. It's quiet. After the hedge mazes it feels like walking into a church.

Mark The villagers here are my favorite writing in the game so far. "I bring Lanu water from the spring every morning. It is hers anyway, but she likes being asked." And an old man: "My knees hurt. I pray anyway. Lanu grew the knees, she can listen to them complain." And "The temple is for Haka. The grove was here first." That last one is the Maki Sages' grudge in one line, from an ordinary person. The loremaster told me about a religious split a hundred years old, and here it is still alive in how people talk about where they pray. If I had to guess, the Great Boar is tied to Lanu somehow, a guardian of her forest, and the boars eating the taro is less about a fat pig boss and more about something being wrong with the goddess. Melia's story might be closer to true than Hina thinks.

Mark Saved at the grove totem. "Lanu's Grove," 155 pule, both portraits on the file now. One odd thing: the save says 0:22 of play time, and I've been at this a lot longer than that. Maybe the clock only counts certain things.

Mark East of the grove is another stretch of forest. A merchant stall up top with an old man behind it, a little pond with another Lanu post, four boars, two green Aghoy, and red mushrooms sitting on either side of a chest. Guards. I'm taking the chest.

Mark The mushroom is called 'Ōkole 'Iole. If my Hawaiian is right, that's something like "rat's backside." I'm going to assume that's a joke and move on. This one is a real wall. It heals for 80. Twice in one round, plus 80 and plus 80. Hina: "Lanu's beasts keep healing. That's Nature. It burns easily, though." So there's the hint, and it ties right back to the loremaster: Lanu is every green thing, so her creatures regrow.

Mark Sauté on it, "Weak!", 22, 25, 26 a cast, plus a Burn. But it still out-healed one Sauté a turn, and then it shifted to shadow stance and breathed "a sickly cloud," though "Poison does not take hold" on either of us. Then back to nature stance and plus 80 again.

Mark So I thought about it. When Hina Scolded the boar in the tutorial, it "starts sulking," and a sulking boar didn't do anything until it stopped. I had her Scold the mushroom. "'Ōkole 'Iole starts sulking." And it stopped healing, and Kailo cooked it with three Sautés in a row. "'Ōkole 'Iole falls." Oh, that was satisfying. The tutorial taught me Scold as a cute joke, and twenty minutes later it was the answer to a puzzle fight. That's good design, and I want to say clearly that I worked it out from the fight itself. Also, "Kailo's Strength up!"

Mark The chest: "Found Seer's Shell." No idea what that does yet. My bag shows the stew progress, Taro 2, Ti Leaf, Egg 3, Water, Pork 2, 'Awa Root. Every ingredient says how long it "Lasts" at sea. Taro "Lasts 14 days at sea." Food spoils on voyages. So there's a sailing game coming, and you'll be packing a larder. I'm into that. Each character also has "Bag 3/4" and "Bag 1/4," so carry space is per person.

Mark Back to the grove to save. And I poured water at the grove's post as well, because Kailo would. And that paid off. The woman with the black hair is a "Sage." "3 of Lanu's posts are still dry. Water all five, and I will have something for you." So the cup of water I poured back in the first forest counted. That's a quest that rewards you for doing what the character would do anyway.

Mark I asked her about Haka. "The priests in the village say Haka is her sunlight, walking around in a man's body." "The sun was always hers. A man from over the sea does not get to borrow it because the priests found it easier to preach." "That is why we left the priests, a hundred years ago, and came to live with the trees. The trees have never once changed their minds about her." So she's one of the Maki Sages the loremaster told me about. Here's the other side of the story, from the side that walked away. And the cups: "Lanu is given what feeds her children. Water for the roots, a little taro now and then." "She does not need it. That is not the point. You give to her the way you give to your grandmother." "And she gives back. Wherever you find her post with a cup beside it, there is a spring near that heals. Drink."

Mark Wait. "A little taro now and then." Lanu is given taro. And the boars are digging up the village taro, and Lanu's beasts are the ones in the woods. If I had to guess, somebody stopped giving Lanu her share, and her animals are taking it themselves. Melia's version, a boss boar sending the little ones for taro, might be the truest thing anyone's said. I'm writing that down as my big theory for next time.

Mark I drank from the grove spring. "The party drinks from the cool pond. Everyone is rested." Free healing next to a save point, explained by the world. Great.

Mark Quest log: "The Great Boar," "Stew for the wake," "Lanu's five posts," all open. The Great Boar entry: "Melia told you the Great Boar is the king of the boars in the woods. He has to be beaten before the woods are safe again." That's from Melia's point of view, which I like, but it doesn't tell me where to go, and that's the thing I most need right now.

Mark That's the hour. I walked back to the grove totem and saved one more time, "Lanu's Grove," 155 pule, Kailo and Hina both on the file. This is a good place to stop. We're standing next to a spring that heals, a goddess's post with a full cup, a Sage who's waiting on three more cups, and somewhere up in these woods a Great Boar nobody will tell me the way to.

Mark Next time I want to find the other three of Lanu's posts and see what the Sage has for me, figure out where the Great Boar actually lives, finish the shopping for the stew, and get back to Noelani before dark, because Old Pono's wake is tonight and I'd hate for Kailo to miss it. I also want to know what a Seer's Shell does, and who that merchant up in the east woods is.

Mark Thanks for hanging out with me for this one. See you next episode.

End of episode

What happened

- New Game. Intro cards: an ocean world of scattered islands; a cook and a priestess on a small island in the northeast. Title card "Kulāiwi Village, The last day of Summer."

- Opening scene: Kailo plans stew for Old Pono's wake. Melia reports boars in the taro patch. Hina joins for the fight.

- Fight 1 (tutorial, Kailo and Hina vs Wild Boar A and B): answered "No" to "You do remember how to fight, right?" and got the full tutorial (turn order, stamina, Light/Medium/Strong, mana, Select for odds, Sauté, Defend, Scold, parry meter). Won. Dropped Boar Hide x2. Element slot unlocked.

- After: the third boar spilled the stew. Melia tells the Great Boar story. Kailo decides to remake the stew and confront the Great Boar. Hina goes home ("you know where I live").

- Kulāiwi Village: talked to a villager (Callers in Makua), the Grocer (shop, no money), saved at the totem, villager ("those kids are lucky they have you"). Chief's Hut: Tutori (tutorial kid), Chief Ulu, the Loremaster (Akua, Lanu, Shaka/Haka, Mana), an elder (Pono's friend). Chest: Ti Leaf. Loft: nothing.

- Kailo's House: Noelani gives the stew list: 4 Fish, 3 Egg, 3 Coconut, 2 Pork, 2 'Uala, 2 Akai Lau, 1 'Awapuhi, 1 Māla Shoyu.

- Collected 2 Eggs from hens outside (third hen unreachable behind baskets).

- Kulāiwi Forest (west, pond screen): poured water at a Lanu post. Fight 2 (Kailo alone vs two Wild Boars): boars healed each other with sleep and a truffle; escaped with Kailo at 62/130.

- Hina's House: Hina joins the party for good.

- Fight 3 (vs one Wild Boar): won. Boar Hide. Opened east chest: Noni Pulu. Fight 4 (Papanok): won, parried a six-blow string. 'Awa Tonic. Fight 5 (Papanok): won (Hina accidentally used Noni Pulu on Kailo). Dropped Sauté. Scooped fresh water at the pond. Could not find a way to that screen's north exit.

- Fight 6 (Wild Boar, on the way back): won. No drop shown.

- Took the north exit from the chief's side of the village into the palm-maze forest. Fight 7 (two Wild Boars): first Combo, Pōhuehue, 81 damage. Dropped Sauté. (A Pork also turned up in the bag around here; I missed which drop it was.)

- Next maze: Fight 8 (Wild Boar): won. Third screen: Fight 9 (Green Aghoy): Green Wing. Fight 10 (Blue Aghoy): Blue Wing, 49 pule. Fight 11 (Blue Aghoy, by the inn): 'Awa Root.

- Crossroads Inn: bought 1 Pork (15) and 1 Egg (10). Talked to the innkeeper and the Cook (how the pot works, salt).

- Fight 12 (Blue Aghoy, north of the inn): Noni Pulu.

- Lanu's Grove: talked to two villagers, saved at the totem.

- East forest: Fight 13 ('Ōkole 'Iole): heals 80 a turn; Scold made it sulk, then three Sautés killed it. Chest: Seer's Shell.

- Back to the grove: saved, watered the grove post, met the Sage (quest "Lanu's five posts", 3 still dry), asked about Haka and the cups, drank from the healing pond, checked the quest log, saved again.

- Episode ended in Lanu's Grove, saved in slot 1. Pule 155. Bag: Taro 2, Ti Leaf 1, Egg 3, Water 1, Pork 2, 'Awa Root 1, plus Seer's Shell, Noni Pulu, 'Awa Tonic, Green Wing, Blue Wing, Boar Hide x3, Sauté x2 (elements).

Stuck and confusing

1. Damage numbers on the wrong boar. In the tutorial, the narrator said every hit landed on "Wild Boar A (front, lower on the screen, on the left)", and the Sauté fire burst drew on the lower boar, but the numbers "6" and "12" drew next to the upper boar (shot-171, shot-245). The sleep Zs also drew over the upper boar while the narrator said Boar A was asleep (shot-355). When Boar A died, the lower sprite vanished. Pressed c and the Sauté target confirm (z).

2. "Each hit you land makes the next likelier." Held Select (shift) before and after a Light hit; both times it read "Y HIT, X 93%, A 78%." The odds never changed.

3. A Light attack that Select called "HIT" was dodged. Hina's chain on the forest boar: "Pops up over Wild Boar: Dodge" on her first Light (c) press.

4. Hits with no parry meter. Several blows landed with no meter (Kailo took 16, 6, 17, 19, 20; Hina took 9, 8), often with "Resisted" or "Weak!" next to them. My guess is these are elemental attacks that cannot be parried, but the game never says so. I was using wait between turns when they landed.

5. Tutori and Chief Ulu loop their whole speech if you press A after the last line; I heard the Info speech twice and the Chief's opening line twice.

6. The north exit of the first forest screen (the pond screen). The narrator kept saying "north (its nearest gap 2 left, 6 up)", but the pond meets the left edge and the palms close off the right. I walked the shore and the palm line (walk left/up/right, "toward water", "toward something solid") and found no path. The real way on was the north exit of the other village screen, which nothing pointed me to.

7. Lore page names don't match speech. The loremaster says "Haka", "Mauna", "Moanaku"; the pages added are "Shaka", "Mauga", "Moanatu". He explained Haka/Shaka as dialect, so this is probably on purpose, but the page list reads like typos until you ask.

8. Escape was greyed in the tutorial and active later, with no word on why.

9. Kailo's Poi (Cook) was greyed out after he had used Attack in the same turn. Select said "Taro paste. Recovers 40 HP." Nothing said why it was grey.

10. Hina's battle menu remembered the cursor on Item from an earlier fight; my confirm used her Noni Pulu on Kailo instead of attacking.

11. Combo: Hina said "Don't mess up your half," but only one note bar ("Grow the vine!", five notes) came up. I never saw a separate half for Kailo.

12. After-fight healing. Early fights showed "Kailo feeds everyone" and HP rising. Later results pages showed the same line with HP not moving while I waited, and HP was higher on the field afterward. Pressing confirm during the feed may cut it short; unclear.

13. Pouring water at a post gave no feedback at all the first time. Only the Sage later revealed it counted.

14. The save file shows 0:22 and 0:27 of play time after about an hour of play.

15. The Great Boar quest page doesn't say where to go.

16. Items menu: pressing right on the Ingredients page did not flip to the next category (the header has arrows), so I never saw what the Seer's Shell is.

Design notes

1. The Chrono Cross attack chain (Light 1, Medium 2, Strong 3 stamina, odds on Select) plus a visible FFX-style turn order is a strong core. Every swing has a visible cost in time. Large, praise.

2. Mana that builds from landing hits, and Skills that can push you into red mana debt you pay back with hits, is clever: Skills are never locked, only expensive. Medium, praise.

3. The parry meter, with a button per blow type and a perfect-parry counterattack, turns defense into a rhythm game. Each monster has its own beat (boar slow strong-strong-light, Aghoy seven fast lights). Large, praise.

4. Elemental attacks bypass the parry meter with no explanation. A one-line tutorial note or a different visual cue would save confusion. Medium.

5. Minigame Skills (mash for Scold, L-R beat for Escape, note lane for the combo) keep you leaning in. Medium, praise.

6. Scold, introduced as a joke, became the solution to the 'Ōkole 'Iole fight (sulking stops its healing). The game teaches a tool early and then asks for it. Large, praise.

7. Enemies change stance mid-fight, and their weakness changes with them, but the only signal is a scrolling text line. A stance icon on the enemy would make this readable. Medium.

8. The full-chain timeline penalty is very harsh when solo: a 7-stamina chain gave the two boars six turns in a row. That makes Hina's "you can't do this alone" true, which is good, but a new player may read it as unfair. Small.

9. Visible enemies on the map, no random encounters. Small, praise.

10. Stats grow by use (Perception, Endurance, Strength ups), no EXP. Fits the "magic is motion" idea. Small, praise.

11. Totems as save and revival points ("tell the Akua what happened") and posts with healing springs make the save system part of the faith of the world. Medium, praise.

12. The lore system (pages that write themselves when a word comes up) is excellent for a world this dense, and the Haka/Shaka dialect detail is lovely once explained. Medium, praise.

13. Navigation: nothing points the player from the village to the true forest path; the first forest screen's north exit appears reachable but isn't. A villager line or sign would fix it. Medium.

14. Damage numbers drawing over the wrong enemy in multi-enemy fights. Medium (it makes targeting look wrong).

15. Battle menu cursor memory across fights caused a wrong action. Small.

16. Repeating NPC speeches when you press A at the end. Small.

17. The writing is the best thing in the game so far: dry, warm, specific (Hina's lines, the grove villagers, the Sage). Large, praise.

18. Food that "lasts N days at sea" and a per-character bag hint at a voyage game with supply planning. Small, praise (promise).

19. The cooking pot rules are explained by a cook at an inn instead of a menu, and the rule that salt never ruins a dish encourages experimenting. Small, praise.

Story and characters

The story so far is small and personal, which I like: a cook trying to remake a funeral stew after boars wrecked it, on the last day of summer. Under that there's a religious split a hundred years old, between the village priests who gave Lanu's sun to Haka (a Buddha-like teacher from the west) and the Maki Sages who left for the woods. The boars, Lanu's creatures and the missing taro offerings seem to be tied together. Two people Kailo leans on are leaving or gone: his dad "left on his adventure," and Hina leaves soon on a pilgrimage for a promotion. The tone mixes warmth, dry humor and grief well.

- Kailo: the cook, warm, practical, takes care of everyone ("Nobody fights on an empty stomach"). Feeds the household since his dad left. Leans on people more than he admits.

- Hina: the priestess, from Kota Emas, an outsider in the village. Dry and bossy, cares through insults ("You're hopeless, aren't you? Well, you need a healer anyway"). Leaving soon on a pilgrimage. The best-written character so far.

- Melia: Kailo's cousin, about eight, raised as his sister. Brave, wants to fight, has a sling. Her Great Boar story may be truer than Hina thinks.

- Noelani: Kailo's cousin, a little younger, the responsible one. Runs the house, helps cook the stew.

- Chief Ulu: kindly, notices Kailo's work. Tutori's grandpa, I think.

- Tutori: the tutorial kid, a light fourth-wall joke that works.

- Loremaster: practices both faiths, gives the big lore in a human voice.

- The Sage: a Maki Sage in Lanu's Grove, firm and warm. Gives the post quest.

- Old Pono: died; a fisherman; the wake is tonight. His friend fished the reef with him for fifty years.

- Kailo's dad: absent, "left on his adventure."

- Ama: old woman by the harbor who sells fishing supplies; named only.

Predictions

1. The island doesn't stay "untouched by the troubles of the wider world" past the opening. Open (said because the intro line is the classic setup).

2. Somebody close to Kailo died, maybe his parents. Wrong: Old Pono died, and Kailo's dad "left on his adventure" (Chief Ulu).

3. Hina is the priestess from the intro and Kailo is the cook. Right (the battle menus, Chief Ulu's "promotion", the loremaster's "young priestess").

4. Noelani is Kailo's sister. Half right: a cousin raised as a sibling (lore page).

5. The game wants me to try the woods alone first and fail. Right: two boars healed each other faster than Kailo could hurt them; I escaped and went for Hina.

6. Kailo will end up following his dad or Hina off the island. Open.

7. Old Pono's death and the Callers of Makua (who talk to the dead) will connect. Open.

8. Element slots are how characters grow. Partly right: slots unlock after fights and elements drop as loot, but stats also grow by use.

9. The stew for the wake is the first real recipe, cooked at Noelani's fire. Open.

10. The Great Boar is tied to Lanu, and the boars are taking the taro because Lanu's share stopped being given. Open (supported by the Sage: "Water for the roots, a little taro now and then," and Hina: "Lanu's beasts").

11. The "take Mana from a beaten champion" belief from the south will become a villain's idea. Open.

The booklet

Never opened. I came close at the first forest's north exit, but trying the other village screen solved it.

Review so far

Nuitai is trying to be a warm, small-scale 16-bit RPG in a Polynesian world, built on Chrono Cross's attack chains and element grid, Final Fantasy X's visible turn order and Super Mario RPG's timed inputs. In the first hour it mostly gets there. The battle system is the star: every swing costs time you can see, mana comes from moving, skills can put you in debt, and the parry lanes give every monster a rhythm to learn, with a counterattack for a perfect read. The 'Ōkole 'Iole fight, where a joke move from the tutorial turned out to be the answer, is the kind of moment that makes you trust a designer. The writing is dry, warm and specific, and the faith and history of the island come through ordinary people instead of lectures.

What doesn't work yet is mostly legibility: damage numbers drawn over the wrong enemy, attacks that can't be parried with no explanation, stance changes you only learn from a scrolling line, a forest exit that looks reachable but isn't, and nothing telling you where the Great Boar is. None of these are deep problems; they're all fixable with a cue or a line of dialogue.

Would I recommend it today? Yes, to anyone who likes Chrono Cross or Mario RPG and is patient with a little roughness. The combat is fresh and the world is worth living in.

My notes for next time

People:

- Kailo, me. Cook. Fire and water stances (Lelua heading; fire shows Sauté, water shows WaveGrd, "Take 60% damage in place of an ally"). Skill menu: Cook (Poi, "Taro paste. Recovers 40 HP"). Dad "left on his adventure."

- Hina, priestess from Kota Emas, in the party for good now. Stance heading Māla Hula (pink flower and sun). Heal, Scold (mash; makes enemies sulk, sulking stops them acting and healing). Leaves soon on a pilgrimage, "earned the promotion" (Chief Ulu).

- Melia, cousin, about 8, "sister." Told me: "The Great Boar lives at the top of the woods, and he's the boss of all the boars. He sends the little ones down to steal taro for him."

- Noelani, cousin, runs the house, cooking the stew with me. Ask her "How many ingredients do I have?" Also offers to hold pule and "A bigger wallet."

- Chief Ulu: "Bring your stew to Old Pono's wake tonight." Tutori's grandpa, I think.

- Loremaster: Lanu is the Akua of Māla Iki, "every green thing." Priests gave her sun to Haka (Shaka in Kota Emas) a hundred years ago; the Maki Sages walked off into the Lost Woods. Other gods: Mauna (cook fire), Moanaku (out past the reef). Mana: "In a body that sits still it sleeps. Get up and move, and it wakes." "In the south they say you can take it from a beaten champion."

- The Sage in Lanu's Grove: "3 of Lanu's posts are still dry. Water all five, and I will have something for you." Cups: "Wherever you find her post with a cup beside it, there is a spring near that heals."

- Callers in Makua "talk to the dead." Ama by the harbor sells fishing supplies. Hunting lodge sells weapons and elements. School on the second floor of the temple, "the tall hale in the grass north of the harbor." I haven't found the harbor, temple, or lodge.

Places:

- Kulāiwi Village: two screens. West screen: Kailo's House (left hale), Hina's House (right hale), hens. East screen: market (Grocer), totem, Chief's Hut (Loremaster, Tutori, chest taken), taro patch.

- North of the west screen: Kulāiwi Forest pond screen (Lanu post watered, chests taken, north exit unreachable).

- North of the east screen: palm maze, then a second maze with boars and a dock/bridge on the east edge (not explored), then a third with Aghoy birds, then the Crossroads (Crossroads Inn; west and south exits not explored; chest on a little island in a pool; a straw-hat figure by a chest the narrator called "a monster").

- North of the Crossroads: Lanu's Grove (totem, healing pond, Lanu post watered, the Sage). East of the grove: forest with a merchant stall, another Lanu post by a small pond, boars, Aghoy, more mushrooms, a chest taken (Seer's Shell). Its east exit not explored.

Rules I learned:

- Attack: Y Light 1 stamina, X Medium 2, A Strong 3; 7 stamina. B backs out and keeps your turn, so you can attack and then cast. Bigger chains push you further down the turn order.

- Mana: 7 marks, built by landing hits and by Defend; Sauté costs 1. Red marks are mana debt from a Skill.

- Parry: lanes Y/X/A; press each blow's own button in the yellow zone; all parried means a counterattack. Elemental attacks ("Resisted", "Weak!") don't seem to come through the meter.

- Combo: both at full mana and side by side on the turn order, press right on the command menu. Pōhuehue: nature vine, note lane.

- Stances: enemies shift stance mid-fight. Fire beats nature (Sauté is "Weak!" on nature-stance boars and on the mushroom). Kailo's basic hits are resisted by the Papanok.

- Nature creatures heal big; Scold them first, then burn them.

- Totems save and revive; Lanu posts take a cup of water; there's a healing spring near each post. Scoop water at any pond.

- Hens give eggs; they refill over time.

- Cooking pot: recipe first, then by type (meat + vegetable = stew, fruit alone = bowl), salt with one thing makes the preserved version; salt never ruins a dish.

- Food lasts a set number of days at sea.

Stew list still missing: 4 Fish, 3 Coconut, 2 'Uala, 2 Akai Lau, 1 'Awapuhi, 1 Māla Shoyu (I have 2 Pork and 3 Egg). The Grocer sells 'Uala Seed and Akai Seed but not the plants. Fish probably means fishing (Ama).

Theories: Lanu isn't getting her taro, so her animals are taking it. The Great Boar is Lanu's, not just a fat pig. Hina's pilgrimage and Kailo's dad's adventure will pull Kailo off the island.

To do next: find the other three Lanu posts (I've watered the pond-screen post and the grove post; there's one by the pond in the east forest), see the Sage's reward, find where the Great Boar is (try the dock east of the second maze, the Crossroads' west and south roads, and the east forest's exit), find the harbor and Ama for fishing, find out what the Seer's Shell does, and get the stew done before dark.

Checked after the episode

- Tutori's line that the hunting lodge sells elements was behind Frankie's 11/22 decision (no shop sells elements); fixed in the game the same day. The booklet line about the lodge was fixed before the episode.

- The lore page names that differ from speech (Haka and Shaka, Mauna and Mauga, Moanaku and Moanatu) are dialect, on purpose, as the loremaster explains.

- The rest of the confusing list goes to Kevin's bug pass, not here: Mark does not hunt for bugs.
